messages:
incident-bot: P1 INCIDENT — High 95th-percentile generation latency originating in eu-west1 since ~09:12 UTC. Auto-spillover engaged to us-central. Several customers on premium tier seeing timeouts and elevated costs due to fallback model selection. Paging on-call (morgan) and infra.
morgan: on it. paging: arjun + samantha. can someone post quick impact numbers and whether customers are actually timing out or just slower?

arjun: digging into routing logs now — initial hypothesis: eu-west1 low capacity triggered spillover policy, routing selected a fallback model 'large-v2-q4' from tier2 that is heavier than primary. That caused cache pressure / OOM retries in us-central pools, which then kicked more requests back to other regions -> feedback loop.

samantha: customer reports: increased response times, some 504s. Using support dashboard: approx 12k affected requests since 09:12, error rate bumped to 8% for premium routes.

lee: re: logs, here's a sampled routing decision trace for a single request_id (redacted):
```json
{
  "request_id": "r-7a9c3f2",
  "origin_region": "eu-west1",
  "policy_version": "routes-v14",
  "decision_path": ["eu-west1->spillover","us-central-tier2"],
  "selected_model": "large-v2-q4",
  "fallback_reason": "region_capacity_low",
  "node_pool": "us-central-dedicated-2"
}
```

arjun: interesting — note the policy_version. routes-v14 introduced a change to model_compatibility fallbacks where quantized variants were not filtered when falling across regions. That probably allowed a model incompatible with the target GPU/quant layout, leading to many runtime terminations.

natalie: quick mitigation idea: disable cross-region spillover for premium routes (keep local-only failover) and fail open to smaller models instead of tier2. Can we flip that safely?

carter: I can push a temporary policy change. Proposed command (runbook):
```bash
# disable spillover for premium route group
redwoodctl routing update --policy routes-v14 --set "spillover.premium.enabled=false" --reason "incident: disable cross-region spillover"
```

deploy-bot: Action queued: apply routing patch to routes-v14 (dry-run pass). Will apply in 15s if no objections.

morgan: do it. also add short-circuit to prefer compatible-models list when spilling (if we can config that quick). we want smaller quantized models, not larger ones.

arjun: running log correlation for OOMs — filter: exit_code 137 on us-central nodes, lots of kernel OOM kills starting 09:14. Sample process exit snippet:
```
[09:14:22] node-id: uc-21-k0 container: gen-worker pid: 1245 exit_code:137 memory: 48GB/32GB OOM
[09:14:23] node-id: uc-21-k1 container: gen-worker pid: 1356 exit_code:137 memory: 49GB/32GB OOM
```

samantha: customer impact update: two enterprise customers reported degraded SLAs; support escalation to CSMs started. ETA to containment?

lee: after routing patch, spillover disabled for premium. early telemetry: traffic no longer spilling to us-central, eu-west1 queues still high but latencies stabilizing ~95th down from 3.8s to 1.6s in the last 6 minutes. error rate trending down.

incident-bot: Mitigation: routing patch applied by deploy-bot at 09:22 UTC — spillover disabled for premium routes. Auto-scaling triggered for eu-west1 dedicated pools (+20% capacity), manual scale requested for canary nodes.

carter: confirming: removed cross-region spillover, and added temporary additional compatibility filter: only models with compatibility_tag:eu-quant present. This prevents selection of large-v2-q4 across regions.

arjun: hypothesis summary (in-thread):
- root cause: policy change (routes-v14) loosened model compatibility checks for cross-region fallbacks.
- mechanism: spillover selected a larger incompatible model in us-central -> OOMs -> node churn -> further spillover -> cascade.
- impact: ~12k requests affected, 8% error spike, partial SLA breach for premium customers for ~10 minutes.

natalie: timeline notes for RCA:
- 09:12 UTC: eu-west1 CPU/GPU contended, auto-spillover engaged (routes-v14 behavior).
- 09:13 UTC: first OOMs observed on us-central gen workers.
- 09:14–09:18 UTC: cascading misroutes as capacity flaps.
- 09:20 UTC: mitigation patch queued.
- 09:22 UTC: patch applied; spillover disabled for premium; eu-west1 autoscale completed partial uplift.
- 09:30 UTC: latencies returned to acceptable range, secondary monitoring in effect.

morgan: allocation for postmortem: owner: arjun (root cause + policy fix), reviewer: lee, mitigations owner: samantha (runbook updates + customer comms). Oncall handoff: carter will take next 2h watch.

oncall-2nd: taking handoff. please ping if anything re-escalates. I will validate autoscale behavior and run a synthetic load against eu-west1 to ensure no further misroute.

ops-runbooks-bot: Follow-ups queued: update runbook 'spillover-policy' to include model_compatibility enforcement across regions; add a synthetic test that simulates region saturation and validates fallback model selection.

morgan: customer comms: samantha to coordinate SLO notes + incident summary for CSMs. We should avoid technical jargon in initial customer email but include ETA and actions taken.

carter: small note — we should also consider a short-term feature: prefer smaller model variants on fallback regardless of tier. Add to TODO.

arjun: long-term fixes proposed: stricter compatibility checks in routing engine, backpressure signals from target pools to prevent naive spillover, capacity buffer defaults per region for premium routes, and add canary gating on policy changes that touch model_compatibility.

morgan: agreed. I'll open postmortem ticket and link this thread. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
